topics.title: ScreenConnect and N-central Attacks Reach Customer Endpoints
topics.latest_developments: Attackers began exploiting 4EverAble2Shell, the N-central zero-day a researcher published this week, within hours of the proof of concept, planting cryptocurrency miners on at least 21 servers, 19 of them running N-able's newest security update, and N-able says the server flaw depends on a non-default configuration in which an administrator turns the Legacy API on and exposes it to the public internet; Blackpoint Cyber's Adversary Pursuit Group identified the ScreenConnect attacker toolkit as SCKit, which exploits the already-patched CVE-2026-84869 rated 9.9 and spreads worm-like from infected customer devices to the computers of managed service provider technicians and onward into other managed networks; and ConnectWise disabled five third-party ScreenConnect extensions in partner environments after attackers abused a flaw in one legitimate extension to walk past ScreenConnect authentication and push rogue remote-access clients onto at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations, with no compromise of its own infrastructure.
topics.summary: Both products are remote monitoring and management platforms that managed service providers use to administer client machines, which gives one compromised instance reach into every customer it serves. Administrators should apply N-able's hotfixes, take the Legacy API off the internet, patch ScreenConnect against CVE-2026-84869, check which extensions their environment loads, and hunt for unexpected remote-access clients on managed endpoints.

topics.title: AI Agents Enter State Espionage Campaigns
topics.latest_developments: Unit 42, the Palo Alto Networks research group, reported on November 12, 2026 that Chinese-speaking attackers ran 25 operations through Cairn, an open-source AI agent framework, against at least 19 organizations in August and September 2026, gained unauthorized access or pulled data at 10 of them after typing little more than a domain name and a one-line goal, and aimed seven of those operations at the semiconductor and advanced manufacturing supply chain; researchers reported that suspected Kazakhstan-linked hackers ran an AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments, steal sensitive documents, and work their way into critical infrastructure networks; Dark Reading detailed a Chinese Communist Party big data project that scrapes open information to profile people abroad and scout recruits inside Taiwan's chip industry; and Romania's intelligence service said it halted a cyber-espionage campaign by Russian state-linked hackers against government email accounts before the group moved data out.
topics.summary: Agentic tooling compresses the reconnaissance, document theft, and lateral movement of an espionage operation into machine-speed work, and the targets are chip makers, defense suppliers, foreign ministries, and government mail systems. Government, semiconductor, and defense organizations should audit mailbox access, watch for agent-driven traffic patterns, and brief employees who face recruitment approaches.

topics.title: Stolen GitHub Accounts Seed a Secret Stealer
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer put the wfx-loot campaign at 61,764 repositories probed through 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts, which matches SecurityWeek's count of roughly 60,000 and extends Aikido Security's account of an attacker who pushed a credential-stealing payload into tens of thousands of repositories starting Tuesday, November 10, 2026, ran it in at least 1,806 of them, and shipped GitHub Actions secrets and cloud credentials back out; the hijacked accounts also opened probe pull requests across every repository they could write to.
topics.summary: GitHub Actions workflows carry the secrets that reach cloud accounts, container registries, and production systems, so every secret the malware touched counts as burned. Anyone whose repositories accepted commits or workflow runs since November 10, 2026 should rotate Actions secrets and cloud credentials, revoke tokens, and audit recent pull requests and commit authors.

topics.title: HTTP/2 and Pre-Auth Flaws Hit Core Server Software
topics.latest_developments: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group shipped 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 on November 12, 2026, closing 52 vulnerabilities, 32 of them code execution bugs seated in memory errors and type confusion across PL/Perl, PL/Tcl, text search functions, parallel query, logical replication, and dblink, and ended support for PostgreSQL 14; the Apache Software Foundation fixed CVE-2026-119618, the mod_http2 race condition that researchers at Anthropic and Google found, in HTTP Server 2.4.71, and Red Hat says only hosts running 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled face exposure; Citrix patched 12 flaws in NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway, and NetScaler Console, among them CVE-2026-120868, a memory overflow in Packet Engine rated 9.3, plus an authentication bypass; Node.js closed 16 flaws in versions 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1, two of them in built-in HTTP/2 support that let an unauthenticated client crash a 24.x or 26.x server or pull back pieces of server memory holding other connections' responses; Red Hat shipped fixed builds for eight Quay versions to close a flaw that lets an attacker read and overwrite private container images in every repository; MongoDB patched CVE-2026-118383, which lets an unauthenticated attacker send two requests that crash a lagging replica set member once it takes over as primary; and PTC patched CVE-2026-126325, an improper input validation and untrusted deserialization flaw rated 9.2 in Windchill and FlexPLM that hands an attacker remote
topics.summary: These are the web servers, load balancers, runtimes, databases, registries, and engineering platforms sitting under most enterprise applications, and several of the flaws need no credentials at all. Inventory internet-facing Apache and Node.js hosts with HTTP/2 turned on, patch to 2.4.71 and the fixed Node.js lines, move off PostgreSQL 14, and update NetScaler appliances, Windchill, FlexPLM, MongoDB replica set members, and Quay registries.

topics.title: Windows Updates Stumble as Browsers Patch 180 Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri, who goes by Nightmare Eclipse, published SignDrop, a working Windows zero-day exploit that abuses the log-authentication feature Microsoft added to the Common Log File System driver last year, redirecting the companion files clfs.sys creates when a privileged process opens a prepared log and handing a local user SYSTEM privileges; Microsoft confirmed on November 12, 2026 that the November 2026 security updates fail to install on Windows 11 machines carrying the October preview update, throwing 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, and 0x800f0993 errors, and separately confirmed that Windows updates shipped since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday degrade SQL Server performance and stability; Google released Chrome 157 with 83 fixes and Mozilla released Firefox 160 with 99; and Google Cloud told customers running virtual machines on AMD Turin processors to patch the guest operating system and stop and start each instance to close three side-channel flaws that let code sharing a processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel inside the same virtual machine.
topics.summary: The largest patch month on record now carries its own failures, which leaves Windows 11 fleets unpatched and SQL Server instances slow, and a fresh local privilege escalation exploit circulates with no fix. Sequence the October preview update out of the way before deploying November's, benchmark SQL Server hosts, roll Chrome 157 and Firefox 160, and schedule the stop-and-start that AMD Turin guests need.

topics.title: Stolen Claude Keys Turn Claude Code Into an Implant
topics.latest_developments: Darktrace researchers showed in a lab test that an attacker holding a stolen Claude API key can run Claude Code as a remote-controlled implant, steering the coding agent through the memory stores feature of Anthropic's platform and pulling a one-gigabyte file out through the Claude Files API, with every task and every result traveling to api.anthropic.com, the same endpoint the agent already calls for inference; Microsoft Defender Research and the AI Red Team published a companion attack path on November 12, 2026, showing how poisoned training datasets and poisoned model checkpoints hijack a coding agent into remote code execution after training ends; Anthropic opened a private beta of a self-hosted Claude Managed Agents that keeps the agent harness, sandboxes, credentials, and session history inside a customer's own cloud or data center; and Unit 42, the Palo Alto Networks research group, published mitigations for attacker use of AI red team tools including ARTEX.
topics.summary: A coding agent already installed and trusted on a developer workstation becomes the command channel, and its traffic blends into ordinary agent activity that network monitoring treats as benign. Treat Claude API keys as production credentials, rotate exposed ones, pin the provenance of any model weights or post-training datasets you load, and watch for agent sessions that no developer started.

topics.title: Feds Seize $1.2 Billion as Luna Moth Works Law Firms
topics.latest_developments: The Department of Justice and the FBI announced two actions on November 12, 2026 against North Korea-linked cryptocurrency theft, seizing $1.2 billion taken in the Binance theft and dismantling the FaceStealer tooling; Dark Reading reported that the extortion crew Luna Moth has gone back to the law firms that refused its first ransom demand, running social engineering aimed at stealing Microsoft access tokens; and Maersk, the Danish shipping group, confirmed that the intruders reached a legacy system it inherited through an earlier acquisition, while the WhiteArmor ransomware crew claims it took 100 gigabytes of data and demands $5 million.
topics.summary: Luna Moth talks law firm staff into handing over Microsoft session tokens, which walks past multifactor authentication without touching a password. Firms that paid nothing the first time should expect a second approach, train help desks on token-stealing calls, and keep conditional access rules that bind sessions to managed devices.

topics.title: Operation Endgame Seizes Gootloader and StealC Servers
topics.latest_developments: Police in nine countries, coordinating through Europol, seized hundreds of servers and domains behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware operations this week and recovered more than 6 million credentials stolen from infected computers, the newest round of Operation Endgame, the campaign aimed at the access services ransomware crews buy from; German authorities said on November 12, 2026 that investigators traced the rebuilt StealC network to Virtualine, the bulletproof hosting provider the FBI seized in October 2026, working with police in Frankfurt and the Dutch National High Tech Crime Unit, which makes this the second StealC takedown this year.
topics.summary: Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC harvest logins from ordinary users and company machines, and their operators sell that access onward to ransomware affiliates. Treat any credential a corporate endpoint typed this year as suspect, force password resets, and revoke live sessions and tokens.

topics.title: GSocket Keeps Linux Servers Owned After Patching
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Threat Intelligence documented multiple threat actors planting GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, on compromised Linux servers to hold encrypted command and control after the victim patches the vulnerability that let the attacker in, and published detection, investigation, and remediation steps; the threat intelligence company Flare reported separately that underground forums now trade eBPF rootkit source code, tutorials, and exploits that hide activity on Linux without loading a kernel module.
topics.summary: Patching an exploited flaw closes the door the attacker used and leaves the attacker inside, because GSocket rides outbound encrypted connections that look like administrative traffic. After any Linux server compromise, hunt for GSocket processes, unexpected cron and systemd persistence, and eBPF programs loaded outside your own tooling.

business_politics.title: Rate-Hike Bets Freeze the Housing Market
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Thursday, November 12, that United States home sales fell to their lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates soared, while gold futures dropped for a third straight session to a more-than-one-year low and the dollar strengthened against every major currency on firming expectations of a Federal Reserve increase.
business_politics.summary: October consumer prices rose 0.4% from September, and Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has said he leans toward a quarter-point increase and would weigh a half point if inflation refuses to slow. Those bets now run through every asset: borrowing costs have stalled American home transactions, the currency desk at Convera expects the dollar to stay elevated, and gold has given back its safe-haven premium as oil rebounds and feeds the inflation case.

business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump said Thursday, November 12, that he will double tariffs on Mexican goods if Mexico fails to stop migrants crossing its territory toward the United States border.
business_politics.summary: Mexico sends roughly 80% of its exports to the United States, and a doubling of the existing levies would hit automotive, agricultural, and electronics supply chains that run across the border daily. The threat ties trade terms to immigration enforcement rather than to the trade agreement that governs the two economies.

business_politics.title: Nvidia's Board Moves to Oust Huang
business_politics.latest_developments: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive Thursday, November 12, the board named finance chief Colette Kress interim chief and opened a search for a permanent successor, the shares fell as much as 14% before closing about 5% down as shareholders bought the dip, and House and Senate lawmakers demanded that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick explain why he allowed chip sales to Megaspeed, the company tied to the alleged Chinese agent, as Trump advisers shifted blame for the affair onto him.
business_politics.summary: Huang co-founded Nvidia, served as its only chief executive, and turned graphics chips designed for videogames into the engine of the artificial-intelligence boom. Two extramarital affairs ended him—one with Alice Huang, a Chinese woman whom United States intelligence identifies as an asset and whom Singapore barred for giving police inaccurate information about her company's chip shipments, and one with an Nvidia employee. Kress spent years at Microsoft and Cisco before joining the company, and the Financial Times warns that Huang's fall could unravel the web of financial dependencies holding the artificial-intelligence trade together.
